references.text: Pilate repeats his declaration of Jesus' innocence for the second time: "I have found no guilt in this man regarding any of the charges you bring against him" ([ref:Luk 23:14|Luke 23:14]).
For the third time, Pilate declares that he finds no fault in Jesus: "What evil has this man done? I have found nothing in him deserving death" ([ref:Luk 23:22|Luke 23:22]).
Also in John's Gospel, Pilate declares that he finds no guilt in Jesus: "I find no fault in him" ([ref:Joh 18:38|John 18:38]).
Pilate goes out to the people and says again, "I find no fault in him," repeating this after they shout "Crucify!" ([ref:Joh 19:4-6|John 19:4-6]).
Also in Matthew's Gospel, Pilate attempts to declare Jesus' innocence and washes his hands: "I am innocent of this man's blood" ([ref:Matt 27:23-24|Matthew 27:23-24]).
Peter confirms Jesus' sinlessness: "He who committed no sin, nor was deceit found in his mouth" ([ref:1 Pet 2:22|1 Peter 2:22]).
Paul emphasizes that Christ was without sin: "For our sake he made him to be sin who knew no sin" ([ref:2 Kor 5:21|2 Corinthians 5:21]).
The prophecy of the suffering servant says, "He had done no violence, and there was no deceit in his mouth" — a prediction of the innocent Messiah ([ref:Jes 53:9|Isaiah 53:9]).

Peter accuses the people: "You denied the Holy and Righteous One and asked to have a murderer granted to you." Pilate wanted to release him, but the people rejected him ([ref:Apg 3:13-14|Acts 3:13-14]).
Paul testifies that they found no grounds for a death sentence against Jesus, yet still asked Pilate to have him executed ([ref:Apg 13:28|Acts 13:28]).
